name: OPA333AIDBVR
title: OPA333, OPA2333: 1.8 V micropower zero-drift CMOS op amps, rail-to-rail in and out
summary: Single (OPA333) and dual (OPA2333) CMOS operational amplifiers that self-correct their offset continuously, giving 10 µV maximum offset and 0.05 µV/°C maximum drift on 17 µA per amplifier. They run from 1.8 V to 5.5 V, accept inputs 0.1 V past either rail without a crossover region, and swing the output within 50 mV of the rails into 10 kΩ. Bandwidth is 350 kHz and 0.1 Hz to 10 Hz noise 1.1 µVPP with no 1/f component. OPA2333AIDR is the dual in the 8-pin SOIC (D) on a 2500-piece reel, marked O2333A.

circuits.title: Input current protection
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower on a single 5 V supply with 5 kΩ in series with the non-inverting input. If the input is driven past a supply rail the input clamp diodes conduct, and the resistor holds that overload current to 10 mA or less. A series resistor is called for once the input can exceed a rail by 0.5 V or more.

circuits.title: Output range down to ground
circuits.description: A follower running from +5 V with its V- pin at ground. A 20 kΩ pull-down from the output to an extra -5 V supply lets the output reach 0 V and a little below. Accuracy holds to -2 mV with 20 kΩ; with 10 kΩ it holds to -10 mV. The pull-down adds several hundred microamps of supply current.

circuits.title: High-side voltage-to-current converter
circuits.description: Turns 0 V to 2 V in into 0 mA to 100 mA sourced from the 5 V supply into a grounded load. Amplifier A drives an N-channel MOSFET so that VIN appears across RS1 (2 kΩ); that current flows through RS2 (470 Ω) from the supply. Amplifier B then drives a P-channel MOSFET so that the drop across RS3 (4.7 Ω) matches the drop across RS2, which multiplies the current by RS2/RS3 into the load. C6 and C7 with R2 and R4 compensate each loop; R3 and R5 isolate the gates.

parts.note: A1 is amplifier A, A2 is amplifier B

notes: Design targets: 5 V dc supply, 0 V to 2 V dc in, 0 mA to 100 mA dc out.

circuits.title: Low-level precision voltage-to-current converter
circuits.description: Turns 0 V to 5 V in into 0 µA to 5 µA through a grounded load. The OPA333 drives the top of RSET; an INA326 instrumentation amplifier, gain set by R1 and R2, measures the voltage across RSET and feeds it back to the op amp's inverting input through R3, with R4 and C1 compensating the loop. The loop forces VIN divided by the INA gain across RSET, and that current flows on through the load and ammeter. VOUT_OPA and VOUT_INA are monitoring points.
notes: Design targets: 5 V dc supply, 0 V to 5 V dc in, 0 µA to 5 µA dc out.

circuits.title: Composite amplifier reference driver
circuits.description: Drives the 4.5 V reference input of an ADS8881 18-bit, 1 MSPS SAR converter. A REF5045 sets the voltage, filtered by 1 kΩ and 1 µF. The OPA333 sets the dc accuracy: it compares the filtered reference with the driven reference node, fed back through 20 kΩ, and integrates the error with 1 µF across it. Through 1 kΩ and 1 µF its output steers a THS4281 follower, which supplies the fast current pulses the converter's reference pin draws; 0.2 Ω and 10 µF load the reference node. A THS4521 fully differential stage with 1 kΩ resistors and a 10 Ω / 10 nF filter drives the converter's inputs.
notes: Design targets: 5 V system supply, 3.3 V converter supply, 1 MSPS, 4.5 V reference, differential input of 4.315 V peak (-0.4 dBFS) at 10 kHz on each input.
Measured THD of the whole system: -110 dB.

circuits.title: Temperature measurement
circuits.description: Conditions a K-type thermocouple (40.7 µV/°C) with cold-junction compensation. A REF3140 makes 4.096 V from +5 V. A divider of R1, R2 and R3 with diode D1, which sits on the isothermal block with the thermocouple terminals, sets a small temperature-dependent offset at the thermocouple's positive lead. The negative lead, loaded by R4, goes through the 549 Ω resistor to the inverting input; R9 sets the gain. R5 and the 200 Ω pot R6 give a zero adjustment at the non-inverting input.
notes: The 549 Ω input resistor carries the name R2, the same as the 2.94 kΩ divider resistor; it is R7 here.

circuits.title: Single op amp bridge amplifier
circuits.description: A resistor bridge of four arms R, excited from VEX and grounded at the bottom, read by one op amp as a difference amplifier. One bridge mid-point goes to the inverting input with R1 as feedback; the other goes to the non-inverting input with a second R1 to VREF, which sets the output's resting level. The amplifier runs from +5 V.
notes: The two resistors named R1 are R1A and R1B here.

circuits.title: Low-side current monitor
circuits.description: Measures load current with a 1 Ω shunt in the load's ground return, where a stray ground-loop resistance also sits. The OPA333 is a difference amplifier across the shunt (R1, R2, R3, R4, gain about 10); its non-inverting side is lifted by the R6/R7 divider from a 3 V REF3130 so the output stays above ground. An ADS1100 16-bit converter (PGA gain 4, 3.0 V full scale, referenced to the same 3 V rail) reads the output against the divider point, and 56 Ω resistors in the I2C lines keep bus noise out. 1% resistors give enough common-mode rejection while ground-loop errors are small; the REF3130 may be left out if the 5 V supply is steady and absolute accuracy is not needed.
notes: The amplifier's supply connections are left unspecified in this circuit.

circuits.title: High-side current monitor
circuits.description: Measures load current with a shunt between the supply V+ and the load. The OPA333 floats on the supply: its V+ pin is at V+ and its V- pin sits one zener voltage below, the zener rated for the amplifier's supply (5.1 V for OPA333). The shunt's low side reaches the non-inverting input through R1 (10 kΩ, current limiting); the inverting input sits at the bottom of RG, whose top is at V+. The amplifier drives a P-channel MOSFET (rated for the supply voltage, BSS84 up to 50 V) that passes the RG current down into RL, so the output voltage across RL is ground-referenced. The zener is biased either by RBIAS to ground or by a current mirror of two N-channel MOSFETs (FDG6301N, NTJD4001N or Si1034) fed from +5 V through a resistor.

parts.note: one of the two bias options
dual N-MOSFET, the other bias option
dual N-MOSFET, the other bias option

notes: RBIAS and the Q2/Q3 mirror are alternatives; one of them is fitted.

circuits.title: Thermistor measurement
circuits.description: A bridge from a 3 V cell: 1 MΩ over 1 MΩ on one side, 60 kΩ over an NTC thermistor on the other. The op amp's non-inverting input takes the fixed mid-point; the thermistor side's mid-point drives the inverting input, with 100 kΩ from the output back to it, so the output moves with the thermistor's resistance.
notes: The amplifier's supply connections are left unspecified in this circuit.

circuits.title: Precision instrumentation amplifier
circuits.description: Three-op-amp instrumentation amplifier. Two OPA333 input stages, each with an R2 from output to inverting input and a common R1 between the two inverting inputs, give gain 1 + 2R2/R1 to the difference while passing common-mode at unity. An INA152 difference amplifier (pins 2, 3 in, 5 sense, 6 out, 1 reference to ground) takes the difference to a single-ended output VO.
notes: The two resistors named R2 are R2A and R2B here.
The amplifiers' supply connections are left unspecified in this circuit.

circuits.title: Single-supply, very low power ECG circuit
circuits.description: An ECG front end on one supply of 2.7 V to 5.5 V with a 0.5 Hz to 150 Hz band and total gain of 1000. Each electrode (RA, LL, LA) enters through 100 kΩ into an OPA2333 follower. R6, R7 and R8 average the three to the Wilson central terminal, which a further follower buffers; the right-leg driver inverts that common-mode signal (R9, R5 with C1) about mid-supply and drives RL through R4. An INA321 (gain 5) takes RA against LA; an OPA2333 integrator (R13, C3) around its reference pin gives the 0.5 Hz high-pass, with a switch to choose ac or dc coupling. The OPA333 adds gain 200 (R12, R14) with C4 setting the 150 Hz low-pass. R10, R11 and C2 make the mid-supply point.

operation.text: OPA333 is one amplifier (SOT-23-5, SC70-5, SOIC-8) and OPA2333 two (VSON-8, SOIC-8, VSSOP-8). All run from 1.8 V to 5.5 V (±0.9 V to ±2.75 V), single or split, and are specified from -40°C to 125°C. They are CMOS, rail-to-rail in and out, unity-gain stable and free of output phase reversal. Automotive OPA333-Q1 and OPA2333-Q1 are separate parts.

The signal path is a continuous 350 kHz amplifier that a self-calibration scheme re-zeroes every 8 μs. The result is a 10 μV maximum offset that barely moves with temperature or age, with no aliasing and no 1/f (flicker) noise. After power is applied the offset takes about 100 μs to reach its specified accuracy.

The common-mode range runs 0.1 V past both rails with no crossover region in between, so CMRR holds across the range and ADC drivers see no differential-linearity error from it. Bias current is about 70 pA typical. Inputs are diode-clamped to the rails; an input beyond the supply is tolerated briefly if its current is held to 10 mA, for example by a series resistor.

At these offset levels, junctions of dissimilar metals at different temperatures add thermocouple voltages of 0.1 μV/°C or more. Keep both inputs' junctions at the same temperature, use low thermoelectric-coefficient joints, keep the amplifier and its input parts away from heat sources such as power supplies, and shield them from moving air such as fan draughts.

On a single supply the output can be pulled to ground or slightly below with a resistor from the output to an extra, more negative supply; about 20 kΩ is the characterized value. With 20 kΩ to -5 V the output stays accurate down to -2 mV; below that it limits and goes non-linear, recovering once driven back above -2 mV. 10 kΩ extends accurate swing to -10 mV. The pull-down costs several hundred microamps of supply current.
The part has no modes beyond on: it runs at any supply from 1.8 V to 5.5 V (±0.9 V to ±2.75 V).

Many parameters are specified from -40°C to 125°C. More than 7 V across the supply can damage the device permanently. A 0.1 μF bypass capacitor close to the supply pins is enough in most cases, and is needed where the supply is noisy or of high impedance.

Keep traces short, use a ground plane, and put surface-mount parts close to the pins with a low-ESR ceramic 0.1 μF capacitor across the supply. Place the gain resistors near the device and near each other, and route input traces as far from supply lines as possible. The OPA333 has low susceptibility to RF interference, though strong RF fields can still shift the offset.

The DFN/SON package carries leads on two sides and an exposed leadframe pad underneath. Connect the pad to V- or leave it floating, but solder it to a board pad in every case: it gives the joint its mechanical strength and long-term reliability under temperature cycling, key push and shear. The land pattern's five holes are optional thermal vias from the pad to a copper area. Attachment practice is in TI reports SLUA271 and SCBA017.
The on-chip ESD protection is modest. Shorting the leads together, or keeping the part in conductive foam, while it is stored or handled protects the MOS gates from electrostatic damage.
